name: Dirty Pink
lede: Dirty Pink is a greyed, dull rose, a survey name for a pink with some brown or grey in it.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name comes from the xkcd survey of 2010, and no earlier record exists in our sources [1]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[puce]], about 6 units away [1].

The words have a long life in writing, though. Derek Jarman uses them in *Chroma* to describe what the common garden geranium brings to mind, which is why he prefers the plant's botanical name pelargonium, with its scarlet [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive a color near this swatch appears in 46 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.19 per cent, which is rarer than 64 per cent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 4.2 times the expected rate, and in a painting it most often plays a light [3]. As always these are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].

questions.q: What plant name did Jarman say conjures a dirty pink?
True or false: the name Dirty Pink is recorded in our sources before 1900.

openers: Derek Jarman preferred to say pelargonium, since geranium conjured a dirty pink for him.
